haiku-low.q1: The breach streak reaches 3 and no incident is open for that service and rule. The evaluator then inserts the incident and writes level 1 due now.
haiku-low.q2: Each further breach is appended to breach_log on the open incident. Breaches never page anyone while the incident stays open.
haiku-low.q3: It resolves when the low streak reaches 10 with an incident open. Pending steps are cancelled and resolved notices are pushed. A later breach run opens a new incident row once the breach streak reaches 3.
haiku-low.q4: Level 1 pages immediately. Level 2 pages 5 minutes later if unacknowledged, and level 3 (engineering manager) pages 5 minutes after that.
haiku-low.q5: The worker sends an SMS with the same attempt key. If that also fails, the attempt is marked failed, the next level stays on schedule, and a background retry resends it.
haiku-low.q6: Each person who was sent a page gets a resolved notice, by push or SMS if push fails. Pending escalation steps are cancelled, so escalation stops.
haiku-low.q7: The breach_streak and low_streak counts are stored in the rule_state table per service and rule. A breach resets the low streak, a low reading resets the breach streak, and anything else resets both.
haiku-low.q8: Both insert a claim row for the service, rule and minute with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so only the first wins. Incidents use a partial unique index on open service and rule.
haiku-low.q9: A timer worker, every 5 seconds, claims due steps with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. It locks the incident and pages only if it is still open and unacknowledged.
haiku-low.q10: The paging provider calls a signed webhook with the provider alert id, which sets acknowledged_at on the incident. The timer worker checks acknowledged_at under lock before each page, so later steps stop.
haiku-low.q11: The schedule service is asked at the moment the step runs who holds that level now, not when the incident opened.
haiku-low.q12: Resolution creates one resolution_notices row per sent page attempt, and each page attempt stores its recipient. The notice sender pushes to that recipient.

sonnet.q1: The breach streak reaches 3 (3 consecutive saved breaches: error rate >2% over trailing 5 min with at least 500 requests) and no incident is open for that service and rule.
sonnet.q2: Further breaches are appended to the open incident (breach_log) and never page. No new incident is opened.
sonnet.q3: The incident resolves when the low streak reaches 10 (readings below 1%, checked each minute) while it is open. A breach after resolution creates a new incident row (once the breach streak reaches 3 again).
sonnet.q4: Level 1 primary is paged immediately (push, SMS if push fails). If no ack within 5 minutes, level 2 secondary is paged. If still no ack 5 minutes later, level 3 engineering manager (last level) is paged.
sonnet.q5: If push fails, an SMS is sent with the same attempt key. If SMS also fails, the attempt is marked failed, the next level's step stays scheduled so escalation continues on time, and a background retry (reaper) resends failed/pending attempts with the same attempt key without holding the timer.
sonnet.q6: Each person who was paged (each sent page attempt) gets a resolved notice by push, SMS if push fails. In the same transaction as resolving, pending escalation steps are cancelled so escalation stops.
sonnet.q7: In the state database, in the rule_state table (breach_streak, low_streak, last_eval_minute) per service and rule. A breach resets the low streak; a low reading resets the breach streak; any other reading resets both. Gaps (metrics unavailable) change no streak.
sonnet.q8: Minutes: each evaluator inserts a claim row (evaluations, primary key service, rule, minute) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the first insert wins and the loser skips the minute. Incidents: a partial unique index on (service, rule) where status is open makes a second open incident insert do nothing.
sonnet.q9: The timer worker (wakes every 5 s) claims due escalation_steps with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. For each, it locks the incident row and reads status and acknowledged_at: if resolved or acknowledged, the step is cancelled; if still open and unacknowledged, it looks up the person and creates the page attempt and sends the page.
sonnet.q10: The provider calls a signed webhook with the provider alert id; the webhook maps it to an incident and level and sets acknowledged_at if still null, returning 200. The timer worker checks acknowledged_at under lock before each page and cancels the step if set, so a late timer cannot page after an ack.
sonnet.q11: At the moment the step runs (when the timer worker pages that level), by asking the schedule service who holds that level right now, not when the incident opened. If the schedule service is down, it uses the last recorded answer, or else the configured fallback contact flagged for review.
sonnet.q12: Through the page_attempts rows: at resolution the evaluator creates one resolution_notices row (unique on incident and page attempt) per sent page attempt, and each notice goes to that attempt's recipient.
